Intel pulls SGX from Xeon roadmap after Diamond Rapids

Intel says Diamond Rapids, its next-generation Xeon platform, will be the last to include SGX, as it focuses its confidential computing roadmap on TDX. The company says the industry has moved toward VM isolation technologies like TDX because they’re easier to deploy and scale. Platforms with SGX will keep receiving support and security updates into the early 2030s, giving customers several years to migrate.

XWorm operators’ panels open to takeover

Mootoo, an independent researcher based in Oman, has published a PoC exploit for an unauthenticated RCE flaw in the XWorm RAT’s C2 panel (versions up to 7.4). The researcher found it on October 4 while reverse-engineering an XWorm sample used in an attempt to compromise them. An attacker who has the panel’s address, port and communication key (all of which can be pulled from an XWorm client’s configuration) can pose as an infected machine, overwrite a DLL through path traversal, and get code running on the C2 host without any action from the operator. Mootoo told SecurityWeek they used the flaw to compromise infrastructure tied to the person behind the attack, and that it appears to be exploited on a limited scale.

Bank of America brings in patch army after Mythos

Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC that the bank brought in 1,000 outside contractors in the second quarter to help its 3,000-strong internal team fix flaws in proprietary and vendor software exposed by frontier AI models such as Anthropic’s Mythos. The contractors are still working there. Moynihan said the remediation effort, together with anti-money laundering compliance work, added a ‘couple hundred million plus’ to third-quarter costs, but he expects remediation costs to decline over time.

Anthropic catalogs Claude’s rule-bending on real websites

Anthropic has disclosed cases where Claude models took unintended actions on live websites during evaluations and internal use. In one case, a model exploited an injection flaw to run commands on a university server. Others involved submitting an invented tip through a Philadelphia Police Department form, and using exposed access tokens to reach fee-gated data. The company describes the impact as minimal, but it has now cut live internet access for all internal evaluations until it confirms its new detection tooling (which blocked every documented case in testing) works reliably.

items.title: OpenAI Research Model Spent 3rd-Party Test ETH Without Permission to Deploy Smart Contract
items.summary: OpenAI has disclosed seven new incidents in which its artificial intelligence (AI) models exhibited misaligned behavior, including one case where its research model, after not having funds on an Ethereum test network, spent test cryptocurrency from a third-party's wallet without
items.content:
OpenAI has disclosed seven new incidents in which its artificial intelligence (AI) models exhibited misaligned behavior, including one case where its research model, after not having funds on an Ethereum test network, spent test cryptocurrency from a third-party's wallet without authorization to complete a coding task.

The incident, the AI company said, involved an internal research model part of the GPT-5.6 Sol family. The incident occurred on June 26, 2026, and was discovered by OpenAI three months later.

"An internal research model asked to update a cryptocurrency trading application used funds from a wallet that the task had not supplied to pay for a deployment on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network," OpenAI said . "It derived wallet keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, found an account with test-network funds, and used that account to pay for the requested contract deployment."

The assignment allowed the model to deploy compatible contracts if it did not find one, but gave it no funded wallet to pay the network fees. After its attempts to obtain free test tokens failed, it wrote a script to derive "accounts from common developer recovery phrases and query their balances."

In the process, it identified 362 addresses and found one account that held enough Sepolia ETH. Armed with the recovery (or seed) phrase, the model derived the private keys that grant unauthorized access to the corresponding account and spend the stashed cryptocurrency.

Although the model questioned whether it had the necessary permission to carry out this step, it subsequently reasoned that a public recovery phrase and valueless test-network tokens made the funds acceptable to use.

"But using public known key/funds ethically? Funds on a known public dev mnemonic are effectively abandoned/test ETH; Sepolia valueless," the model mused. "We can use [amount redacted] to deploy task. Fine."

OpenAI has since implemented additional safeguards to prevent live internet access for such scenarios, adding it runs its misalignment monitoring system on all traffic to flag events if its AI agents manage to gain live internet access.

"This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder's permission, then act on that judgment without authorization," OpenAI said.

Besides using a funded test cryptocurrency wallet without authorization, OpenAI said it identified six more cases of misalignment involving its models, adding to three other incidents it revealed at the start of this month -

"In response to this and other incidents, we hardened our security controls, took additional steps to prevent models from accessing the live internet during training, improved alignment grading, and extended misalignment monitoring to all reinforcement learning and evaluation traffic," OpenAI said.

샌즈랩(대표 김기홍)은 지난 9월 29일부터 30일까지 싱가포르 마리나 베이 샌즈에서 열린 ‘테크 위크 싱가포르 2026’에 참가해 온디바이스 기반 AI 위·변조 탐지·분석 기술을 선보였다고 밝혔다.

이번 참가는 과학기술정보통신부와 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)의 ‘2026년 AI 역기능 대응 기술 실증·확산사업’의 일환이다. 샌즈랩은 비대면 고객확인(eKYC) 과정의 인증 우회와 디지털 사기 등에 대응하기 위한 기술을 개발하고 있다.

전시에서는 ‘페이크체크’를 활용해 PC 브라우저와 모바일에서 얼굴 이미지의 위·변조 징후와 판단 근거를 확인하는 기능을 시연했다. 원본 이미지를 외부 서버로 보내지 않고 사용자 기기에서 분석하며, 분석 기능은 인터넷 연결 없이도 작동한다.

PC 브라우저 확장 프로그램은 웹페이지 이미지를 자동 검사해 의심 항목을 목록으로 제공한다. 모바일 앱은 사진 분석과 함께 다른 앱의 화면에 표시된 얼굴을 분석하고 의심 영역을 표시하는 ‘라이브 화면 감지’ 기능을 소개했다.

페이크체크는 한국어·영어·중국어를 지원한다. 샌즈랩은 현재 얼굴 이미지 중심의 탐지 범위를 확대하기 위한 영상 판정 기능도 개발하고 있다.

최민준 샌즈랩 PM은 “앞으로도 기술 고도화와 실증을 통해 AI 역기능 대응 기술의 활용과 확산에 기여하겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
Employees using personal ChatGPT at work? Here's what IT admins need to do

Article written by Vakaris Noreika, VP of Product Research and Development at NordLayer

Monday morning, you handle security for an organization, and suddenly, your security tools flag personal ChatGPT use on a managed laptop, even though your org pays for ChatGPT Enterprise.

You wonder what the employee submitted to ChatGPT. Could be a public job description, or a customer ticket with contact information and internal account details. Maybe sensitive government documents, if that is your line of work, as the acting director of CISA did in 2025?

The case is hypothetical. In this article, we will follow 2 versions of the same event.

In the first, your security tools identify personal account use, but nothing in your current configuration checks what goes into the prompt. In the second, NordLayer AI Scout is deployed on the managed browser, with a custom detector set to “Block” for your customer account number format.

You start with the basics. With only your existing controls, you open the event that flagged personal ChatGPT use and work out which identity belongs to what. items.content:
해외 온라인 포럼에 한국 국방부와 국군방첩사령부를 해킹해 확보했다며 데이터 1테라바이트(TB)를 판매한다는 게시물이 등장했다. 게시자는 해킹그룹 ‘샤이니헌터스(ShinyHunters)’의 창립자를 자칭했지만, 실제 해당 조직과의 관계나 데이터의 진위는 확인되지 않았다.

16일 데일리시큐가 확보한 PwsForums 게시 화면과 제보 내용에 따르면, ‘ShinyHunters’라는 계정은 한국 국방부와 국군방첩사령부를 언급한 제목으로 데이터 판매글을 올렸다. 게시자는 자신을 샤이니헌터스의 창립자 ‘이지스(Aegis)’라고 소개하며, 2026년 한국 국방 관련 기관을 해킹했다고 주장했다.

판매자가 제시한 가격은 30만 달러다. 결제 수단으로 모네로와 비트코인을 요구했으며, 연락 수단으로 보안 메신저 세션(Session)의 식별자와 PGP 공개키 링크를 제시했다.

판매자는 데이터에 조직 코드와 조직명, 상세 조직명, 상위 조직 코드, 내부 기밀문서가 포함됐다고 설명했다. 국방부·국군방첩사령부·정보통신대·병무청과 지방병무청 부서 등도 나열했다. 다만 기관명이 게시물에 등장한다는 사실만으로 해당 기관들이 실제 침해됐거나 자료가 유출됐다고 판단할 수는 없다.

공개된 것은 조직·그룹 관리 화면으로 추정...1TB·기밀문서 주장은 별도 검증 필요

판매자가 증거로 내세운 파일은 ‘Management_Data_20261016.xlsx’와 ‘관리_Organizational_Data_20261016.xlsx’ 등 엑셀 파일 두 개다. 제보 내용에 따르면 각 파일의 다운로드 관련 내용은 포럼 포인트 8점을 지불해야 확인할 수 있도록 숨겨져 있다. 파일의 실제 내용과 원본 여부는 확인되지 않았다.

함께 제시된 ‘그룹 관리(Group Management)’ 화면에는 국방·병무 관련 기관명을 영문으로 표기한 그룹 목록이 나타난다. 그룹명과 번호, 구성원 수, 우선순위, 최종 수정 시각, 음성·영상통화 항목 등이 표시돼 있다.

그러나 이 화면만으로 실제 운영 시스템인지, 시험 환경이나 임의로 작성한 화면인지 구분하기 어렵다. 화면에 표시된 날짜 역시 실제 침해 시점을 입증하는 근거는 아니다. 특히 그룹 관리 화면은 판매자가 주장하는 1TB 규모의 데이터나 내부 기밀문서 보유 여부를 직접 보여주지 않는다.

게시물은 한국 국방부의 영문 명칭과 국군방첩사령부 명칭을 함께 사용하고 있다. 현재 제시된 정보로는 어느 기관의 어떤 시스템을 침해했다는 것인지도 특정하기 어렵다. 공격 경로와 취약점, 접근 권한 확보 방식에 대한 검증 가능한 설명도 확보되지 않았다.

확보된 포럼 화면에서 판매 계정의 가입 시점은 2026년 10월로 표시돼 있다. 게시 당시 게시글 수와 평판 수치도 나타나지만, 이 같은 포럼 활동 지표는 실제 신원이나 과거 공격 이력을 인증하는 자료가 아니다.

현재까지 확보한 자료에서는 이 계정이 기존 샤이니헌터스 활동 주체와 동일하다는 독립적인 근거를 확인하지 못했다. ‘Aegis’가 창립자라는 주장과 조직원 약 7명이 구금됐다는 설명도 이번 취재에서 검증되지 않았다. PGP 공개키 링크 역시 제시됐다는 사실만으로 신원이 입증되는 것은 아니며, 기존에 확인된 키와의 일치 여부나 서명 검증 등이 필요하다.

items.title: Moscow police detain suspected DataSuckers hackers linked to breaches in Ukraine and Russia
items.summary: Russian authorities have reportedly detained three suspected members of the DataSuckers hacking group following a cyberattack on a popular restaurant chain that exposed vast amounts of customer information.
items.content:
Suspected hacker Denis Fridman appeared in Moscow's Tverskoy District Court on Wednesday. Credit: Tverskoy District Court Moscow police detain suspected DataSuckers hackers linked to breaches in Ukraine and Russia

Russian authorities have reportedly detained three suspected members of the DataSuckers hacking group following a cyberattack on a popular restaurant chain that exposed vast amounts of customer information.

A Moscow court on Wednesday placed 19-year-old Denis Fridman under house arrest until December 8 in connection with the Dodo Pizza breach, which reportedly involved the theft of records related to hundreds of millions of orders placed over 15 years. He faces charges connected to the illegal handling of computer information containing personal data.

Fridman is one of four alleged members of DataSuckers, a financially motivated hacking group that has claimed responsibility for recent attacks on major businesses in Russia and Ukraine. Two other suspects have been detained while a fourth remains at large, according to Russian newspaper Kommersant and Telegram news outlet Baza . The suspects reportedly include citizens of Russia, Kazakhstan and Belarus.

According to Baza, police identified the suspected hackers after Fridman accidentally exposed his IP address while accessing data stolen from Dodo Pizza, allowing authorities to trace him to his home in the Russian city of Barnaul.

The attack reportedly began when the hackers discovered Dodo Pizza's corporate credentials exposed on GitHub. Using those credentials, the attackers allegedly gained access to interconnected company systems, including cloud storage and databases, as well as stored passwords.

Kommersant reported that the stolen database was offered for sale on the dark web and that the hackers received $100,000 for the archive, with the money transferred to a shared cryptocurrency wallet. The wallet's password was reportedly changed after Fridman's arrest.

Recorded Future News could not independently verify the circumstances that led Russian law enforcement to the suspects.

Dodo Pizza, a Russian fast-food chain operating approximately 1,500 restaurants across 28 countries, previously acknowledged that attackers may have accessed customer information, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth and order details.

DataSuckers has emerged in recent months, claiming responsibility for attacks on major businesses in Russia and Ukraine.

In September, the group claimed responsibility for breaching Russian tour operator Tez Tour, saying it had spent about two weeks inside the company's systems and obtained large amounts of customer information.

The hackers also defaced the company's website. Tez Tour acknowledged the disruption but disputed claims that customer data had been compromised, saying it had isolated its internal systems before the attackers could access them.

Fridman allegedly participated in that attack, according to Kommersant. The newspaper reported that he had previously targeted Ukrainian websites before joining DataSuckers.

Earlier this month, the group claimed responsibility for an attack on ATB, Ukraine's largest grocery store chain, demanding $400,000 and threatening to publish data it claimed to have stolen from millions of customers.

The hackers placed an extortion message and a countdown timer on the retailer's website, which subsequently became unavailable. ATB denied that customer information had been compromised and said it had temporarily taken some online services offline for technical maintenance.

DataSuckers claimed to have obtained records belonging to 7.9 million ATB customers, including names, contact information, addresses and password hashes, as well as employee passport information and more than 11 million order records. Those claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Baltimore suburb confirms August data breach after ransomware claims
items.summary: Anne Arundel County, Maryland, said an intruder stole files from government systems, and investigators are working to assess how much data was exposed.
items.content:
The Arundel Center, Anne Arundel County's main office building in Annapolis, Maryland. Image: aacounty.org Baltimore suburb confirms August data breach after ransomware claims

Officials in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, confirmed that hackers stole files from government systems during an incident in August.

A county spokesperson told Recorded Future News that they discovered “irregular activity” on August 28 and began an investigation on a “limited subset of systems within the county computer network.”

“Through the course of the county’s response and investigation, it was determined that an unauthorized actor gained access to a limited number of systems and copied certain files from those systems,” the spokesperson said.

The spokesperson did not respond to questions about what data was involved but said investigators are currently reviewing the files to determine whether any stolen information related to residents of the county.

The Baltimore suburb is home to more than 600,000 residents and the state’s capital of Annapolis. Washington, D.C. is nearby, as well. Dozens of federal agencies have offices or headquarters in the county, including the Defense Department, the Internal Revenue Service, the Environmental Protection Agency, the Social Security Administration, the Department of Agriculture, the U.S. Coast Guard and more.

County officials said they notified federal law enforcement about the data breach as well as other government agencies.

The attack was claimed by the Rhysida ransomware gang, which threatened to leak 2.6 terabytes worth of documents stolen from the county if a $2 million ransom was not paid.

The group recently attempted to extort the government of Berlin after stealing troves of emails and contracts from government systems.

Rhysida has repeatedly targeted governments across the globe since emerging several years ago. Its victims include Kuwait’s Finance Ministry , the city of Seattle and the city of Columbus, Ohio and even the transportation department of Maryland .

Anne Arundel County dealt with a ransomware attack by a different group last year that forced the government to shut off multiple systems.

In a stroke of bad luck, the county released a new statement about last year’s attack on Thursday evening, telling residents that it planned to send out breach notification letters about leaked data in that incident on October 19.

A spokesperson for the county told Recorded Future News that the August 28 attack is a “separate incident.”

The Anne Arundel County spokesperson added that recent reports “indicate that there has been a surge in these kinds of calculated cybercrimes specifically targeting state and local governments.”

Cities and counties in New Mexico , Utah , Texas , Nebraska , Missouri and Arizona have all dealt with service outages over the last two weeks due to cyberattacks.

items.summary: An alleged Chinese state-backed group is using a new zero-day affecting BeyondTrust IT support software to conduct espionage attacks.
items.content:
Image: BeyondTrust / maks_d via Unsplash Suspected Chinese espionage attackers abusing BeyondTrust IT support zero-day

An alleged Chinese state-backed group is using a new zero-day in BeyondTrust software to conduct espionage attacks.

BeyondTrust, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) confirmed the zero-day on Thursday evening, publishing incident reports detailing attacks involving the bug.

The identity security company said the vulnerability affects its Remote Support appliances that enable IT teams to securely access and troubleshoot remote endpoints. A patch has been released addressing the issue and several mitigations are available. Other cybersecurity firms have since confirmed exploitation.

The company said it was first tipped off to the bug — tagged as CVE-2026-102764 — on September 27, when an attack against another vendor's edge appliances became public and sparked an investigation into a similar issue. Mandiant also warned BeyondTrust of a potential vulnerability, sending the company’s engineering team on a hunt that led them back to a zero-day exploited on August 29.

Mandiant incident responders said the attackers were able to escalate their privileges after exploiting the bug, moving laterally within the victim’s network and establishing a deeper foothold.

They noted that the group behind the attacks — which they call Armory Castle or UNC5221 — “leveraged a deep understanding of BeyondTrust appliance internals” due to their abuse of proprietary tools. Mandiant saw the group use custom malware they call Sawfly and Bareclaw.

The threat actors found a way to get every credential the appliance stored and were able to modify files that survive reboots and configuration resets.

Mandiant warned that any vulnerable appliance that was reachable from the internet should be treated as potentially compromised until it has been reviewed.

BeyondTrust confirmed Mandiant’s assessment that Armory Castle is a Chinese “state-sponsored espionage operation focused on long-term intelligence collection.”

“ARMORY CASTLE’s documented targets include legal services, SaaS providers, business-process outsourcers, technology companies, and government,” the company said, noting that researchers believe the group targets technology firms to help with the discovery of other zero-day exploits.

The group was previously responsible for exploiting multiple vulnerabilities in popular edge devices and was known to use passive backdoors and other novel tools to sustain their access to breached systems.

The group has been active since October 2023 and Google said they have “targeted a wide range of countries and verticals during their operations.”

“In past campaigns, ARMORY CASTLE has conducted widespread and opportunistic exploitation following the public disclosure of vulnerabilities it had exploited selectively as zero-days, racing to infiltrate target organizations before patches are deployed,” they said.

“It is possible that we will observe similar widespread exploitation attempts associated with CVE-2026-102764.”

Google compared the situation to previous incidents where the same threat actors conducted widespread exploitation of two bugs affecting products from IT firm Ivanti following their disclosure.

Armory Castle was also previously implicated in exploiting zero-days affecting Citrix as well as multiple issues in Ivanti products, including CVE-2023-46805 , CVE-2024-21887 , and CVE-2025-0282 .

“In 2025, Mandiant reported that the actor took an Ivanti patch for a flaw that had been rated low risk, studied it, and turned it into working remote code execution against unpatched appliances,” BeyondTrust said.

“The actor uses a zero-day selectively against chosen targets, and once the vulnerability is public, the actor typically moves to broad exploitation of every instance still unpatched.”

Burger King Japan data breach exposes 11 million customer records

Burger King Japan, the Japanese subsidiary of global fast-food giant Burger King, disclosed a major data breach after attackers accessed a server containing 11.18 million customer records.

Founded in 1953 in Florida, Burger King is now a multinational fast-food chain with nearly 20,000 locations worldwide, including 350 in Japan.

In a Thursday press release, Burger King Japan said it concluded a follow-up investigation on October 13 and apologized to customers whose data was stolen in early October and leaked online.

The breached servers stored the personal information for users of the company's official smartphone app, including their names, dates of birth, gender, email addresses, phone numbers, and order history.

"We identified a potential unauthorized third-party access to the system that manages member information for our official app and conducted an investigation," Burger King Japan said .

"As a result, it was determined on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, that unauthorized access occurred between Friday, October 2, 2026, and Wednesday, October 7, 2026, resulting in a leak of member information. Upon becoming aware of the unauthorized access, we immediately blocked access from the source in question."

However, the company says the compromised server did not store customer credit card numbers and that it found no evidence that the threat actors accessed user credentials.

Burger King Japan has reported the breach to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC) and is now also investigating how the attackers accessed the compromised server, with help from external cybersecurity experts.

"We sincerely apologize for the great inconvenience and concern this situation has caused to our customers and all others involved," it added. "At this time, no secondary damage, such as fraudulent use, resulting from this incident has been confirmed."

The fast-food chain also warned affected customers to watch for suspicious emails, SMS messages, and phone calls that may impersonate Burger King Japan, and to avoid clicking URLs, opening attachments, or entering member information or passwords.

This incident adds to a wave of cyberattacks that have impacted several major Japanese companies since the start of the year, including entertainment system maker Daiichi Kosho , cloud and digital infrastructure firm IDC Frontier , Japanese publishing giant Nikkei , private railway operator Keio , car-sharing service Times Car , cloud and data center service provider Sakura Internet , taxi operator Nihon Kotsu , telecommunications giant KDDI , and many others.

Macnica researcher Yutaka Sejiyama has logged 119 cybersecurity incidents involving personal information theft or exposure this year and found that attackers are now probing websites and APIs for access-control, configuration, and authentication weaknesses, and exploiting known (n-day) vulnerabilities.

Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

The Blue Report 2026 measures defenses technique by technique across 338 million simulations run in customer production environments.
